cleared.check: Whether the PoolManager-only replay can fail: the reference interpreter was given a planted MULMOD fault (result off by one when the modulus is 2^256-1, the modulus FullMath.mulDiv uses) and run on 15 matched MegaETH swaps.
cleared.result: All 15 became unmatched, so a wrong 512 bit product on the swap path shows in the frame, log and storage comparisons. The deployed PoolManager runtime on 143, 4326 and 999 equals the build of this checkout byte for byte except the 20 bytes of the immutable address (eth_getCode, 24,009 bytes each), so the program counters of the build's jump map apply to the deployed code.

cleared.check: Whole-transaction replays (every contract, not only the PoolManager) of the first 270 Monad and MegaETH transactions, to see whether the narrower PoolManager-only method hides anything.
cleared.result: Mismatches in the whole-transaction replay traced to the reference interpreter having no gas: a router frame that is given zero gas, and an aggregator that prices the trade with GAS, GASPRICE and BASEFEE. In every such case the PoolManager frames and storage matched once the outside frames were taken from the call tree, which is why the PoolManager-only method was used. This is a limit of the tool, not a difference of the networks.

leads.question: Which producer evidence can exist for the branches with no mined instance on Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM: clear() of an exact credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319, jump pc 3614), transferFrom and burn by a spender with a finite or infinite allowance or as operator (src/ERC6909.sol:35-38, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:15-19, pcs 722 and 1105), approve, donate (no Donate log in any of the three windows), afterAdd/RemoveLiquidityReturnDelta on Monad and MegaETH, swaps that end exactly on an initialized tick, and the large-number branches of FullMath and SqrtPriceMath (pcs 22358, 23900, 23942)?
leads.why: For these sides the networks have produced no block, so only simulated calls (which on Monad never run native code and on MegaETH and HyperEVM run a different program from the producer) speak to them. A deployment test that mines one transaction per side on each of the three networks before liquidity arrives would give the producer evidence that does not exist today.

leads.question: Do the Monad PositionManager or routers ever call clear()? 3,507 replayed Monad transactions, including all 747 ModifyLiquidity transactions of 300,000 blocks and 1,500 random swap-only transactions, hold no successful clear frame.
leads.why: clear credits nothing and moves no tokens; without a mined instance the compiled path of its delta update has no producer evidence on Monad.

leadResults.answer: Every mined instance that was found matches. Of the 83 jump sides cycle 12 newly covered, mined instances exist for the hook self-call sides (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:172, 217, 253, 293) and the parseReturn side of callHookWithReturnDelta (Hooks.sol:163) on all three networks, and for Hooks.sol:233 on HyperEVM only: Monad 5 sides, MegaETH 7, HyperEVM 8. Replays: Monad 3,507 of 3,507 matched, MegaETH 1,566 of 1,567 and HyperEVM 2,762 of 2,763, the one set aside on each being the PoolManager's own deployment. Named families with mined, matched instances are listed in cleared. With no mined instance on any of the three: clear of an exact credit, transferFrom (none at all), burn or transfer by a spender with an allowance or as operator (every burn was by the owner), approve, donate, the SqrtPriceMath overflow fallback and the FullMath 512 bit branch at pc 22358, and swaps ending exactly on an initialized tick. afterAdd/RemoveLiquidityReturnDelta hooks have 3 transactions each, on HyperEVM only. Those sides have no producer evidence (see leads). On MegaETH the frames compared are those of a revm re-execution, and the logs and storage are the sequencer's; on HyperEVM the receipts are the validator's and the storage is a replay client's.

settleFor: 12 Monad transactions in the 3,507 replayed (23 frames, 10 of them with native value), all matched in frames, logs and storage. clear: no successful clear frame in any of the 3,507 Monad replays, which include every ModifyLiquidity transaction of blocks 124691690 to 124991689 and 1,500 random swap-only transactions, so clear remains without a mined instance on Monad. The scan was by call tree, not by router call data.
